name: sas_derivation_v1
description: Short Authentication String derivation for out-of-band Signal verification. Derivation: take the canonical encoding of the preimage object, SHA-256 it, read the first four bytes big-endian as an unsigned 32-bit integer, reduce modulo 1000000, and format as six decimal digits with leading zeros. The SAS is a human comparison aid over public identifiers; it is not a secret, not a credential, and confers no authority. Provenance note: this derivation is defined here, it is not a pinned external standard.
security_limitation: This SAS does NOT defend against an attacker who can choose one of the identifiers that feed the preimage. Six decimal digits is a 1000000-wide space, so an attacker free to vary device_public_id (or any other preimage input under their control) can search for a value whose SAS equals a target and find one quickly; an independent reviewer ground a collision against a published SAS in under seven seconds on ordinary hardware. The code therefore only detects accidental mismatch and a passive observer, not an active attacker who selects an identifier. Do not treat a matching SAS as proof of identity, and do not use it to gate an effect. Strengthening this (longer codes, a commitment step, or binding to values no party can choose after the fact) is an owner design decision tracked as DISC-029 against the SAS-consuming issues; it is deliberately not changed here.
